title: The Imperfect Subjunctive: Stem and Endings

sections.title: What you know
sections.content: You know the forms *tuviera* and *hablara* from B1 Unit 4, and the imperfect subjunctive after a past verb, as in *Quería que vinieras*, from B1 Unit 38. From B1 Unit 4 you also know how to build it: take the *ellos* form of the preterite, remove *-ron* and add the endings. This lesson puts the whole system in one place, shows the *-ra* and *-se* endings side by side, and groups the irregular verbs so that you can see why they look the way they do.

sections.title: The stem comes from the preterite
sections.content: Every verb follows the same steps: the *ellos* form of the preterite, minus *-ron*, plus the endings. *Hablaron* gives *habla-*, *comieron* gives *comie-* and *vivieron* gives *vivie-*. Because the stem comes from the preterite, an irregular preterite passes its irregularity on, and the present tense does not matter: *tengo*, but *tuvieron* gives *tuviera*; *puedo*, but *pudieron* gives *pudiera*.

sections.title: Irregular stems, in groups
rows: tener. Also: hicieron → hiciera (hacer), pudieron → pudiera (poder), quisieron → quisiera (querer), pusieron → pusiera (poner), vinieron → viniera (venir), supieron → supiera (saber), estuvieron → estuviera (estar)
ser and ir share one form
decir. After *j* the *i* of *-ieron* disappears. Also: trajeron → trajera (traer), condujeron → condujera (conducir)
leer. The *i* between two vowels becomes *y*. Also: oyeron → oyera (oír), construyeron → construyera (construir)
pedir. The vowel change of the preterite stays. Also: durmieron → durmiera (dormir), sintieron → sintiera (sentir), siguieron → siguiera (seguir)
dar and ver have short stems

items.spanish: Mi jefe quería que termináramos el informe hoy.
items.english: My boss wanted us to finish the report today.

items.spanish: Nos pidieron que trajéramos los documentos.
items.english: They asked us to bring the documents.

items.spanish: Le dije que leyese el contrato con cuidado.
items.english: I told him to read the contract carefully.

items.spanish: No creía que ellos dijeran la verdad.
items.english: I did not think they were telling the truth.
If I could, I would sleep late.

sections.content: In the *nosotros* form the stress falls on the vowel before the ending, so it always carries an accent: *habláramos*, *comiéramos*, *tuviésemos*. The commonest mistake is to treat an irregular verb as a regular one: *trajera*, not *trayera*, and *dijera*, not *dijiera*. If you know the preterite *ellos* form, you can build the subjunctive.
